candidates.lesson_subject: ICAP request/response offload: WAD connection pools, queue saturation, and failure semantics
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiOS proxy-mode ICAP REQMOD/RESPMOD offload through WAD workers; max-connections pool, per-worker allocation, request queue and timeout; fail-open/fail-closed profile behavior
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: client HTTP/HTTPS session -> firewall policy with proxy inspection and ICAP profile -> WAD worker obtains pooled ICAP connection -> request/response adaptation service -> returned verdict/content -> client session continues or fails
candidates.failure_class: ICAP server slow/no response holds connection slots; WAD workers exhaust shared connection allowance; queued request exceeds queue timeout and client session is dropped
candidates.evidence_pattern: ICAP connection error log; WAD icap_client and conn_pool stats; ICAP remote-server status; WAD worker health; TCP/1344 packet capture; (nil) source-port pointer is a socket-reference symptom, not a routing diagnosis
candidates.remediation_path: Measure ICAP service latency and WAD worker load; set max-connections no lower than wad-worker-count and size to server concurrency; enable health checks; decide request-failure/response-failure bypass versus error deliberately; test queue behavior and ICAP server capacity before increasing from 100 to 500
candidates.question_fingerprint: Distinguish ICAP queue saturation from a policy mismatch using worker pool occupancy, server response latency, queue timeout and socket evidence
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Three-lane client/FortiGate-WAD/ICAP-server topology with WAD worker pool, bounded connection pool, waiting queue and timeout/drop branch
candidates.uniqueness_reason: No ICAP/content-adaptation/WAD-queue lesson exists in the 357 historical lesson fingerprints.

candidates.lesson_subject: Workspace Mode onboarding exception: adding devices and policy packages without an ADOM lock
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiManager 8.0 global device-policy-package-lock-allow-add flag relaxes ADOM lock only for creation of new managed devices and policy packages in Workspace mode; created objects are automatically locked
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: global CLI flag enable -> enter unlocked Workspace-mode ADOM -> create device or package -> FortiManager creates object and acquires object lock -> later edits/install follow normal lock and permission rules
candidates.failure_class: confusing object-creation exception with global-policy assignment/install permission; Workspace Mode automatic global policy assignment can fail with no-write-permission on affected 7.6.8 builds
candidates.evidence_pattern: config system global flag; ADOM lock state; device/package lock owner; install preview and task result; global/local ADOM assignment log
candidates.remediation_path: Enable only the 8.0.0 global flag when required; verify the newly created object is locked; do not treat the setting as a global lock bypass; for the documented 7.6.8 global assignment defect lock both Global and Local ADOMs or reinstall manually and apply the release-specific fix
candidates.question_fingerprint: Identify exactly which lock is bypassed and which lock is automatically acquired after device/package creation
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiManager control-plane diagram with Global flag, unlocked ADOM, device/package creation branch, auto-lock on each object, and separate later edit/install permission gate

candidates.lesson_subject: Dynamic MAC learning limits: FDB admission, violation logging, shutdown timer and static-entry boundaries
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSwitch dynamic FDB learning limit 1-128 per physical interface or VLAN; zero means unlimited; static entries excluded; mac-aging-interval; one violation per interface/VLAN; optional log-mac-limit-violations and physical-port shutdown action
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: source MAC frame arrives -> dynamic learning eligibility checked -> FDB entry counted against port/VLAN limit -> violation logged once -> physical port shutdown action held until timer expiry or explicit reset
candidates.failure_class: shutdown action appears configured but port remains up because mac-violation-timer=0 disables shutdown; no event appears because global violation logging is disabled
candidates.evidence_pattern: get switch mac-limit-violations all; diagnose switch physical-ports list; execute log display; compare static/dynamic FDB entries; inspect mac-violation-timer and log-mac-limit-violations
candidates.remediation_path: Set nonzero mac-violation-timer, enable global log-mac-limit-violations and per-interface log-mac-event, set learning-limit and learning-limit-action on a physical port, then reset the violation record after remediation; static MAC entries do not consume the limit
candidates.question_fingerprint: Explain why a FortiSwitch port remains active despite learning-limit-action shutdown and distinguish dynamic from static MAC accounting
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Layer-2 port/VLAN FDB admission diagram with dynamic MAC counter, static-entry bypass, violation logger, shutdown latch and timer/reset release
candidates.uniqueness_reason: No prior FortiSwitch lesson covers dynamic MAC FDB admission limits, violation latches or shutdown timer behavior.

candidates.lesson_subject: LDAP simple-bind signing failures: distinguishing credentials from transport integrity and migrating to LDAPS/STARTTLS
candidates.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC-F LDAP directory connection uses LDAP simple bind; Security Protocol None/SSL/STARTTLS, default ports 389/636/389, CA keystore trust, Connect by Name for certificate identity, independent from Winbind Kerberos/SMB domain join
candidates.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: FortiNAC-F Validate Credentials -> TCP LDAP simple bind -> domain-controller signing policy -> bind result code -> user/group search and scheduled directory sync
candidates.failure_class: unsigned simple bind over TCP 389 rejected by a domain controller requiring LDAP signing; result code 8 Strong(er) authentication required, distinct from result code 49/52e invalid credentials
candidates.evidence_pattern: ldapsearch -x result code 8 versus 49/52e; packet capture bindResponse result 8 and DC reset; Windows Directory Service events 2888/2889; Winbind domain join may still succeed
candidates.remediation_path: Use LDAPS 636 or STARTTLS 389; select the domain-controller FQDN matching the server certificate and Connect by Name; import issuing CA into FortiNAC-F keystore; validate credentials and directory sync; do not weaken domain-controller signing except as a temporary approved workaround
candidates.question_fingerprint: Explain why a successful Winbind domain join and reachable TCP 389 do not prove that FortiNAC-F LDAP simple bind satisfies signing policy
candidates.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiNAC-F-to-AD domain controller sequence diagram showing TCP connect, unsigned bind, LDAP result 8, and alternate LDAPS/STARTTLS trust path
candidates.uniqueness_reason: Historical FortiNAC-F lessons cover EAP-TLS certificates, MDM, NetFlow and LDAP group data; none covers LDAP simple-bind signing enforcement and transport upgrade.
